title: Stochastic Lead-Time Aware Autoscaling Policy for Dedicated Fleets
creator: Ariana Chen
description: Design and implement an autoscaling policy that factors in stochastic request lead times (queueing and warmup) to produce stable scale decisions for dedicated GPU fleets while enforcing contractual throughput floors and cost-aware ceilings. The goal is to reduce oscillation and failed scale events during bursty traffic and model warmup periods.
background: Current autoscalers rely on relatively short-window throughput and latency percentiles. Dedicated fleets see hard lead times due to model KV warmups, node assignment delays, and prefetch lanes. These introduce delayed feedback into the controller and cause overshoot or reactive oscillations. Existing tickets (predictive warmup, headroom controllers) address parts of this, but we need a combined stochastic lead-time model integrated into the policy compiler and rollout engine for Dedicated capacity.
goals: Produce scale actions that respect contract throughput floors (per-tenant guaranteed throughput) with <1% SLA violation during 95th percentile burst scenarios
Limit unnecessary scale-ups by at least 30% vs baseline reactive scaler during KV-warmup-heavy workloads
Ensure scale-downs incur no more than 10% increased cold-start latency for long-tail requests
Provide clear observability hooks (predicted lead time, confidence bands, reason codes) for Console and SLO dashboards
proposal_summary: Create a two-part policy: (1) a stochastic lead-time estimator that learns per-model/per-sku warmup and assignment latency distributions from historical traces, and (2) a decision engine that fuses demand forecasts, the lead-time distribution, and contractual floor/ceiling constraints to output scale intents with safety envelopes. The engine will be pluggable into the existing policy compiler and will emit human-readable reason codes for rollouts and cost analysis.
target_metrics: scale_action_stability_score (novel internal metric to measure oscillation)
algorithm_overview: We will implement a hybrid controller combining: (A) a probabilistic lead-time predictor (mixture-of-exponentials fitted per model+sku) that outputs a lead_time_cdf(t) and uncertainty; (B) an MPC-like decision rule that optimizes for minimizing SLA breach probability over a lookahead horizon given cost penalties for scale-ups and contractual penalties for missed throughput; (C) a conservative safety filter that enforces floors/ceilings, slew rates, and emergency backoff on repeated failures. Forecasting uses short-window autoregressive smoothing with heavy-tail handling to avoid being misled by extreme spikes.
safety_limits: Safety enforced via layered guards: (1) Contract floor: never allow predicted committed throughput < contracted_min without opening a fallback (throttle or route to hosted) and creating an incident; (2) Slew limits: hard cap on absolute change in node count per minute (configurable per-sku); (3) Cooldown windows: require a minimum stabilization period after scale-up before another scale-down on the same tenant; (4) Cost ceiling: a soft limit mapped to billing budgets that triggers alternate routing before aggressive scale-ups; (5) Rollback policy: automatic rollback to last-known-good policy on repeated failed scale attempts with retained diagnostic snapshot.
rollout_plan: Build offline simulator using recorded traces and synthetic burst scenarios (owner: Miguel)
Implement lead-time estimator and expose read-only metrics in telemetry (owner: Lina Park)
Integrate decision engine into policy compiler as an optional policy type (feature-flagged) (owner: Backend team)
Canary rollout to internal Dedicated test fleet with a single low-risk tenant, monitor scale_action_stability_score and committed_throughput_utilization (2 weeks)
Gradual rollout to production dedicated pools with progressive tenant enrollment and SLA monitoring
acceptance_criteria: Simulator shows >=30% reduction in scale-ups vs baseline under KV-warmup traces while maintaining contracted throughput
Lead-time estimator converges to stable distributions within 24 hours of model introduction for 90% of models in dedicated test pool
Console surfaces predicted lead time and reason code for each scale decision and SLO dashboard shows <1% contracted_throughput SLA breaches during canary
Feature flag allows immediate rollback with zero customer-visible request loss in testing environment
Automated tests for safety guards and rollback path included in CI
tasks: T1 - Define lead-time schema and telemetry (metrics/labels/events)
T2 - Implement offline estimator from historical traces and unit tests
T3 - Build simulator harness (trace replay + noise injection)
T4 - Implement decision engine library and policy compiler hooks
T5 - Add safety filter primitives (slew, cooldown, floors/ceilings)
T6 - Instrument Console with reason codes and predicted lead-time panels
T7 - Run canary and small-batch production rollouts, capture metrics
T8 - Document runbook and incident playbook for scale failures
